requirement:
The generated coverage subchapter MUST make coverage-collection and
post-suite-checking guidance available under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`, without requiring
separate authored content.
rationale:
structural: No clause of `requirements.test-coverage.index.guidance` prescribes how the implementation is built. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. I found no implementation roots.

The obligations are all about observable output:
- "MUST make coverage-collection and post-suite-checking guidance available under `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance`". This says what the generated subchapter contains. Any generator, template or embedded static text that produced the same guidance would satisfy it, so the mechanism is discretionary.
- "without requiring separate authored content". This says the project author doesn't have to write anything. It does not say which code builds the text.

The `{cite}` of `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance` only points to the declaration that defines the guidance. That declaration's content belongs to its own assessment.

The requirement already has a `{test}` edge to `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]`. That test covers the behavior. No `{impl}` evidence is needed.

behavioral: The subject has one behavioral obligation. The generated coverage subchapter MUST carry the coverage-collection and post-suite-checking guidance that `requirements.test-coverage.check.guidance` describes. It MUST do so without separate authored content.

The marked test is `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]`. It covers the obligation in these ways:

- **Guidance present.** The test runs `populate_in` on a fixture book and then asserts that the generated `coverage.content` contains each of the following strings:
  - The commands `habeas test`, `habeas coverage -- --workspace` and `habeas coverage-check`.
  - "after it succeeds,\nrun `habeas coverage-check` as a separate step". This matches the clause to run `habeas coverage-check` as a separate step after a successful `habeas coverage -- --workspace` run.
  - "`habeas test` collects coverage for the whole workspace,\nthen checks it". This matches the clause that `habeas test` runs collection and then checking, in order.
  - "static validation test needs no prior coverage". This matches the clause that the static validation test does not require current collected coverage.
- **No authored content.** The fixture has no authored coverage chapter, only the parent "Requirements index" chapter and a "Guide" sub-item. The test asserts that the generated chapter has `source_path` set to `None` and path `reports/coverage.md`. It also asserts that the page does not still contain the `:::{coverage-index}` directive. The guidance therefore comes from generation rather than authored text.
- **Both numbering modes.** The loop runs with and without a section number. In both runs the guidance assertions hold and the chapter is present under the parent.

I found no gap. Requiring "under check.guidance" is a cited context requirement, and I did not reassess its own tests.

Habeas's bundled agent instructions and setup-generated coverage documentation
MUST recommend running `habeas coverage-check` after a successful full-workspace
instrumented nextest run using `habeas coverage -- --workspace`, as a separate
CI step. They MUST document `habeas test` as the command running collection and
The static validation test MUST NOT require current collected execution
coverage or validate exception applicability against current runtime gaps.
Those checks belong to the post-suite coverage command. Coverage checking
MUST NOT depend on running the static validation test last.
